analysis.title: GS Novak - GS U.S. Industrials & Materials | CPI | prime | A&D from here (9 Nov 2026)
key_insights: GS desk (Ryan Novak) is more constructive than in a long time on aerospace, especially the aftermarket but across the subsector. Q3 aftermarket trends were mixed versus recent years but solid, and the desk sees room for secular acceleration (e.g. LEAP) even in a cyclical slowdown.

Desk views GE as the aerospace bellwether with lowered expectations after underperforming the market, industrials and its sector this year. The desk has repeatedly called GE valuation extended. After a 10-point P/E pullback and a 7-point EV/EBITDA pullback, the multiple may now be more reasonable.
Desk likes HONA as a deeper-value turnaround and BA with patience, since free cash flow estimates have rebased.

Desk is positive on defense primes (LMT, GD, NOC, LHX, RTX) but notes recent outperformance from the bid for defensives raises the bar. It calls Q3 the cleanest quarter across the primes it can remember, and sees the budget path likely higher, not lower, in the short and medium term.

Desk highlights LHX as a stock with catalysts: potential new management, changes in how financials are presented, Golden Dome and Missile Solutions optionality. It also likes RTX for strong organic growth, idiosyncratic margin potential and a portfolio levered to growth and restocking areas.

On what may have run too far, the desk questions whether the ATI vs. CRS vs. everything gap could pause. HWM, HEI and WWD look more expensive versus GE than normal. TXT caught a fundamental, under-owned bid in the last month but remains inexpensive, and the desk could see it give back gains.
For exposure to both aero and AI, the desk points to BWXT and CW, while remaining neutral to slightly negative on the AI catalyst path.

Prime brokerage data: Industrials was among the worst-performing US sectors and the most net sold last week at -3.3 standard deviations (1-year), driven by long sales and short sales at about 2 to 1. The week's % net selling in US Industrials was the largest since Covid (Apr 2020) and the second largest on record (since 2016).

GS economists estimate October core CPI +0.16% m/m SA, headline +0.21% m/m, and core PCE +0.23% m/m. Year-over-year figures will not be available for most indexes because October 2025 values are missing from last year's government shutdown.

Core CPI details: expected declines in used cars (-1.5%) and car insurance (-0.3%), medical services -0.1% (medical insurance -2.5% on the semiannual source data update), airfares unchanged, OER +0.26% and rent +0.23%. BLS interpolation of shutdown-missing data distorts October seasonal factors and is estimated to add 5bp to seasonally adjusted core CPI, boosting public transportation, apparel and hotels.

Pre-market on 11/9: S&P futures +40bps led by non-tech with NVDA weighing on tech. KOSPI -81bps, Japan +233bps after last week's rout, Germany +60bps, France +20bps. WTI below $90 and Brent below $97 (-100bps) as the President says additional strikes are unlikely despite harsh Rubio comments on Iran's demands. Metals well bid. 10-year yield 4.87%, DXY below 102, Bitcoin flat near $74k.
Week ahead: CPI and PPI are the focus. Earnings pre-market Monday include SGI, RBA, CNH, CECO and FERG, and the desk hosts ORLY CFO and IR at 2pm on 11/9.
